summary: The unit is mostly sound: the nested quotation opens in 24:34 and stays open, the ketiv is in the apparatus, and the English adds nothing. The main fault was 24:38, where 'If not' rendered אִם־לֹא as a conditional and Abraham's quotation was closed at 24:37, so 24:38 read as the servant's own words. Smaller faults: the Rashi summaries at 24:33 and 24:37, the giver of the gifts in 24:35, three senses (silver, gold, כֹּל) and the feminine parse of אִתָּךְ.

patches.value: Rashi: אִם is used in the sense of both אֲשֶׁר and כִּי, as in עַד כִּי יָבֹא שִׁילֹה; and this is what the sages said, that כִּי is used in four senses, one of which is אִי, that is, אִם. The English reads 'until'.
patches.reason: The summary said 'that particle' and omitted אֲשֶׁר; Rashi's four senses belong to כִּי, whose one sense אִי he equates with אִם.
Silver in a list of the master's wealth is 'silver as wealth' (3), not 'costly gift' (6); the context note on this verse also speaks of wealth.

patches.value: Silver as wealth, reckoned by weight.
patches.reason: Matches the corrected sense.
Gold in a list of wealth is 'gold as wealth' (2), not 'costly gift' (5).
Matches the corrected sense.

patches.value: Wayyiqtol 3ms. The subject continues from the blessing, the LORD; the master is the one to whom (לוֹ) the gift is given.
patches.reason: The note said the giver is not named; the master cannot be the giver to himself (לוֹ), so the sense points to the LORD, as in Onkelos.

value.english: The LORD blessed my master greatly
value.literal: and-the-LORD blessed OBJ my-master greatly: the prefix ו has no English; the object marker is not translated.
and-became-great: the wayyiqtol continues the sequence after the qatal of blessing.
and-gave to-him: 'he' keeps the 3ms form; the giver is the one who blessed, and לוֹ is the master.

value.english: flocks and cattle and silver and gold and servants and maidservants and camels and donkeys
value.literal: flocks and-cattle and-silver and-gold and-servants and-maidservants and-camels and-donkeys: a list of eight with ו on each item after the first.

patches.reason: Corrects the phrase note on the giver.

value: The qatal בֵּרַךְ opens the verse; the two wayyiqtol verbs carry the narrative on.
The subject of וַיִּגְדָּל is the master; the subject of וַיִּתֶּן is the one who blessed, the LORD, and לוֹ is the master: he cannot give to himself. The English keeps 'he' for the 3ms verb.
The list is a run of nouns each with ו, the first without; the English 'and' follows the Hebrew.
patches.reason: The note said the Hebrew leaves open whether the LORD or the master gives; לוֹ settles it.

patches.value: The first verb names the LORD; the next two have no named subject, and the English keeps 'he'. The master is the subject of 'became great' and the one to whom the gifts are given.
patches.reason: Aligns the translator's note with the corrected grammar.
2.b.(a) falls under הַכֹּל with the article; here כָּל is in construct before a relative clause: 'all that...'.

patches.value: כֹּל in construct before a relative clause: 'all that is his'.
patches.reason: Matches the corrected sense.

patches.value: My master made me swear, saying, 'You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell.
patches.reason: Abraham's words run on into 24:38 (If not... = 'but rather'); the inner quotation must stay open to the end of 24:38 so that 24:38 is not read as the servant's own words.

patches.value: Rashi: he takes the prohibition as holding on a condition, 'if you do not first go to my father's house, and she is not willing to go after you'. The words state no condition, so the English keeps the plain prohibition.
patches.reason: The summary made the refusal to follow the servant's own ('after me'); Rashi's words are 'after you', and the unwilling one is the woman.

patches.value: Single quotes mark Abraham's words inside the servant's speech; the outer double quotation is left open, and Abraham's quotation runs on into 24:38.
patches.reason: Records that the inner quotation continues into the next verse.

patches.value: Rather, you shall go to my father's house and to my kin, and take a wife for my son.'
patches.reason: אִם־לֹא after a negative command means 'but rather' (Onkelos אֱלָהֵן), not a conditional 'if not'; 'If not,' made the sentence read as a condition with no main clause. The closing single quote ends Abraham's words begun in 24:37.

value.literal: if not: after the negative command of 24:37 it means 'but rather'; Onkelos has אֱלָהֵן.

value.english: you shall go to my father's house
value.literal: to house-of my-father you-go: 'house of my father' is the English 'my father's house'.
and-to my-clan: 'and to' continues the verb 'go'.

value.english: and take a wife for my son
value.literal: and-you-take wife for-my-son: the weqatal continues the instruction.

patches.reason: The new English changed the first fragment.

patches.value: אִם־לֹא after a negative command: 'but rather', as in Onkelos (אֱלָהֵן); the pair is not a conditional here.
patches.reason: The old note read it as a conditional alternative.

value: אִם־לֹא after the prohibition of 24:37 means 'but rather': the servant is to go to the father's house and kin, nowhere else. Onkelos renders it אֱלָהֵן.
תֵּלֵךְ and וְלָקַחְתָּ are 2ms: the servant is addressed as 'you'.
בֵּית אָבִי: the father's household as the place of the bride's family.
Abraham's words, begun in 24:37, continue here; the single quotation closes at the end of this verse.
patches.reason: The first note called it 'if not'; adds the continuation of the quotation.

patches.value: The suffix is pointed like a 2nd feminine singular and the dataset parses it so, but the addressee is the servant, a man; the sense requires the masculine, so the suffix is read as 2ms. English 'you'.
patches.reason: The old note kept the feminine parse and said the gender is left open; the context fixes it as masculine.

value: The speech of Abraham is in single quotes inside the servant's speech; the outer double quotation stays open.
הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי is hitpael: 'walk about'; with לְפָנָיו it reads 'walk before him'.
The two future clauses: the LORD will send his angel and will make the way prosper; the second is a perfect with waw continuing the future.
The suffix on אִתָּךְ is pointed like a 2nd feminine singular, but the addressee is the servant; it is read as 2ms and the English is 'you'.
patches.reason: Matches the corrected token note.

patches.value: Perfect with waw continuing the future of the promise; the English 'shall' keeps the force of the instruction of 24:38.
patches.reason: The weqatal continues the promise, not only the earlier instruction.

verdicts.comment: The English gives the unnamed passive Ibn Ezra describes: 'there was set'; the qere hofal is translated.
The English takes the words in their plain sense, as Ibn Ezra rules; the food reading is not adopted.
